meta.purpose: The cart permalink layer. A reader who has already decided should be able to put the thing in the basket from this page, not click through a product page and hunt for a button.
meta.verification: This session opened https://www.amazon.com/gp/aws/cart/add.html?AssociateTag=shopnow047c-20&ASIN.1=B0CDY277D3&Quantity.1=1 with a redirect-following fetcher. Amazon responded and redirected to https://www.amazon.com/ap/signin?openid.assoc_handle=amzn_associates_add_to_cart_us with openid.return_to=https://www.amazon.com/associates/addtocart?ASIN.1=B0CDY277D3&Quantity.1=1. So the endpoint is real, the format is accepted by Amazon, and an anonymous fetch lands on a sign-in page — which is the expected behaviour for adding to a cart, and is why this layer cannot be proven to credit a commission from here.
meta.what_is_verified: The endpoint accepts the URL shape and returns an Amazon sign-in redirect with the Associates return path. The five ASINs are the destinations observed this session.
meta.what_is_not_verified: That a completed purchase through these links is credited to shopnow047c-20. That needs the Associates report, and it is still FLG-002.
meta.policy_note: Program Policies 2(b) requires the Associates ID as a parameter on each link to an Amazon Site. That is the 'AssociateTag' parameter here. Encoding and decoding rather than an opaque redirect keeps the destination inspectable, which is what makes it checkable.
meta.automation_note: There is no scraping, no rotation of destinations, and no cloaking. Plain links, written out in full, one per product.
